title: Prism
description: A component system that makes its behaviour inspectable: spring motion, shared overlays, three visual expressions and recorded AI response states.
techStack: React, TypeScript, Spring Physics, Browser Top Layer
status: Component-system release merged; live demos and recorded AI replays

blocks.heading: From components to a system
blocks.body: The interesting part of Prism is no longer an individual button. It is whether inputs, menus, dialogs and asynchronous responses behave like they belong to the same product. I moved the work towards shared behaviour: typed APIs, spring motion, a common overlay layer and visual expressions held to the same interaction contracts.

blocks.heading: Follow an asynchronous answer through the interface

steps.label: Stream contract
steps.detail: An abortable StreamSource yields text, tool calls, tool results, errors and completion. The contract accepts either a real provider adapter or a recording.

steps.label: State transitions
steps.detail: A quiet window avoids flashing a busy state. A stalled stream exposes waiting and cancellation. A settled or replaced run ignores late events.

steps.label: Response surface
steps.detail: The component renders received text, inspectable tool steps, citations and stop/retry controls. A citation is a link only when its source exists.

steps.label: Behaviour checks
steps.detail: The browser suite exercises the response lifecycle. The demo uses retained recordings, including imperfect runs and a labelled injected timeout.

blocks.caption: This is interface engineering around a model response. It does not claim that displaying a citation proves the answer correct.

blocks.heading: Keep the behaviour, change the expression
blocks.context: A different visual language should not require a different keyboard model or props API.

options.label: Separate component implementations
options.detail: Each expression could evolve independently, but behaviour would need to be checked and repaired in several places.

options.label: Shared behaviour with distinct expressions
options.detail: Keep the interaction contract and vary the presentation. Test that contract across the expressions.

blocks.outcome: The expressions become a test of the component system rather than separate galleries. Visual variety has to survive the same behavioural checks.

blocks.heading: Let the browser own the layer
blocks.context: A panel inside a transformed or clipped ancestor can disappear regardless of its z-index. Closing a native overlay immediately also cuts off its exit motion.

options.label: Portals and larger z-index values
options.detail: Move each panel manually and manage its stacking outside the browser top layer.

options.label: Top layer with shared dismissal and presence
options.detail: Use manual popovers and native dialogs, with a shared dismiss stack and spring presence. Prefer CSS anchor positioning where supported, with a measured JavaScript fallback.

blocks.outcome: Escape dismisses the top layer. Closing panels stay mounted through their exit spring. Modal focus return and scroll locking belong to the shared layer, rather than each component inventing them.

blocks.heading: Show the engineering
blocks.body: X-ray makes hit targets, focus order, roles, contrast and springs visible while exploring a component. Its overlay joins the top layer too, so opening a dialog does not hide the inspection tools. This exposes implementation choices; it does not certify accessibility or replace testing.

blocks.heading: Make AI behaviour repeatable
blocks.context: An AI response interface needs to handle waiting, tool calls, partial answers, interruption and failure. A fresh model response on every visit would make those states difficult to compare and introduce a running cost.

options.label: Call a model on every visit
options.detail: Fresh output, but variable timing, variable content and a model bill attached to a public demo.

options.label: Replay recorded local-model events
options.detail: Record real local Ollama output, preserve event timing and feed it through an abortable stream interface.

blocks.outcome: The demo can be stopped, retried and inspected without a paid call. An injected tool timeout is labelled, and a wrong-source run remains visible as a failure. The interface presents response state; it does not verify whether a model claim is true.

blocks.heading: AI interfaces beyond the answer bubble
blocks.body: The AI response component makes tool arguments inspectable, reveals streamed text at an even pace, links citations only when a source exists and announces the completed answer once to screen readers. Latency states and the async button share timing rules for fast starts, slow requests and retry; settled states ignore late results. Token Compose explores a different boundary: a seeded generator produces layouts from a closed token vocabulary, and a validator rejects off-token values. It is deterministic generation, not an LLM choosing a layout, and the validator checks membership rather than taste or contrast.

blocks.heading: What remains
blocks.body: The shadcn-format registry, the next form primitives and a shared OKLCH token contract are follow-ups. They are not presented as available installation paths. Current source files include app/lib/hooks/overlay.ts, anchor.ts and assistant.ts; browser contracts live under tests/.
